verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'dramatic splashdown in the Pacific on Friday'; R2: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; R4: 'Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; R6: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R7: 'splash down off the coast of San Diego, California'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm splashdown location in Pacific Ocean off California/San Diego coast.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific on Friday'; R3: 'Updated April 10, 2026'; R4: 'April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)'; R6: 'April 10, 2026'; R7: 'April 10, 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm date as April 10, 2026 (local/PDT), with R1 specifying Friday.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'SPLASHDOWN! ... at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R6: '8:07 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on exact time and timezone in NASA source and news report.

verifications.claim: 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026 corresponds to 00:07 UTC on April 11.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: R4 explicitly states UTC time on April 11 corresponding to April 10 PDT/EDT, confirming conversion (EDT=UTC-4).

verifications.claim: Artemis II was the first human trip to the moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: 2026 - 1972 = 54 years, matching 'over 50 years'; explicitly first crewed lunar trip since Apollo.
